Clinical details:
Progressive exertional breathlessness. Echo: dilated LV, EF approximately 30%. Normal CT coronary angiogram. ?Aetiology.

Technique:
Cardiac MRI at 1.5 T. Cine SSFP imaging in standard long- and short-axis planes, T2-weighted STIR, native T1 and T2 mapping, post-contrast T1 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement imaging following 0.1 mmol/kg gadobutrol.

Findings:
The left ventricle is moderately dilated with normal wall thickness and severely impaired systolic function due to global hypokinesia. LVEDVi 142 ml/m², LVESVi 101 ml/m², LVEF 29%, LV mass index 74 g/m².

The right ventricle is normal in size with mildly impaired systolic function. RVEDVi 96 ml/m², RVESVi 50 ml/m², RVEF 48%.

The left atrium is moderately dilated. Moderate functional mitral regurgitation (regurgitant fraction 28%) secondary to annular dilatation.

No pericardial effusion. Small bilateral pleural effusions.

Tissue characterisation:
Native T1 1092 ms (local reference range 950–1050 ms at 1.5 T). T2 50 ms (local reference range 42–52 ms). ECV 34% (normal <30%). No myocardial oedema. Raised native T1 and ECV indicate diffuse interstitial expansion.

Late gadolinium enhancement:
Linear mid-wall enhancement of the basal to mid septum, in a non-ischaemic distribution. No subendocardial enhancement to suggest prior infarction. No intracardiac thrombus.

Conclusion:
1. Dilated left ventricle with severely impaired systolic function (LVEF 29%) and mildly impaired right ventricular function.
2. Septal mid-wall fibrosis in a non-ischaemic pattern, in keeping with dilated cardiomyopathy. With the normal CT coronary angiogram, an ischaemic aetiology is effectively excluded.
3. Moderate functional mitral regurgitation.
4. Suggest discussion at the cardiomyopathy MDT.
